title: Python: PEP 695 type-parameter bounds and constraints are not walked
description: Record-only follow-up from GCLI-112's round 3 review (opum-ai/glyph-cli#220, landed 3a422ec1), accepted in DEC-303 (a72) item 3 as N4; ordinary, not on the hold list. A PEP 695 bound or constraint (def h[T: C], def h[T: (A, B)], class K[T: C]) is an expression Python evaluates lazily in the type-parameter scope, but the walker pushes no children of a type_parameter, so a call or name read inside a bound is never recorded as a call site or a class-body use. GCLI-112 only reads the declared names from the list (typeParameterNames); the typeParams null refusal in enumerableBindings is accepted as defensive with no fixture. Not started.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Decide whether a call inside a bound or constraint (def h[T: f()]) is a call site, and in which scope it resolves (the type-parameter scope, lazily)
Fixtures red before and green after, measured against dev by running both; the five-pin delta (the corpus has no PEP 695) identical or reported
